newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso ends firm on auction hopes.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso ends firm on auction hopes.

text.p: The Mexican closed firmer for the second session in a row on Monday as local and foreign dealers sold dollars amid predictions of primary interest rate hikes, traders said.
"The peso closed firmer on momentum carried over from Friday," a trader said.
The benchmark 48-hour peso and its 24-hour stablemate both closed 1.9 centavos firmer at 7.9590/7.9640 and 7.9550/7.9590 per dollar, respectively.
Same-day peso contracts had earlier closed four centavos firmer at 7.9600/7.9650 per dollar.
Dealers forecast an increase of 50-75 basis points on primary Cetes rates at the central bank auction to be held on Tuesday.
"The market discounted a Cetes hike, so the peso firmed up in response," another trader said.
Traders said stable U.S. long bond yields and a buoyant bourse also helped bolster the peso.

Yields on the 30-year U.S. Treasury bond stood at 6.83 percent, marginally up from 6.81 percent in late trade on Friday. The IPC index of leading Mexican stocks was up 0.46 percent at 3,827.35 points when the foreign exchange market closed.
Dealers predicted the peso would trade at similar levels on Tuesday while awaiting the outcome of the primary Cetes auction.
